features.title: Unified agent activity feed
features.summary: Normalizes session, communication, and jj integration events into one durable chronological feed with deduplication, bounded retention, cursor pagination, filtering, search, and provenance.
failureModes: A duplicate delivery is deduplicated by event id instead of appended twice.
Out-of-order timestamps are re-sorted on ingest.
A malformed ingest payload is rejected instead of stored.
Missing sources (no jj coordinator, no communication) leave the feed usable rather than failing.
The retained window is bounded, so old events age out predictably.

externalDependencies.boundary: Optional cross-plugin cordis events (dshfiles/activity/event) plus a bounded backfill request; the timeline never runs jj itself.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Adapters are exercised directly in src/activity-timeline.test.ts; the jj adapter boundary is validated without the coordinator running.

externalDependencies.boundary: Optional cross-plugin cordis events for message and communication-tool activity; no communication state is read directly.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Adapter mapping is unit-tested with fixed payloads.

features.title: Deterministic condensation and attention visibility
features.summary: Collapses routine runs and correlated events into traceable groups while keeping errors, blocked integrations, and attention-required events individually visible; a detailed mode expands every retained event.
features.currentSurface: left-nav: Activity Timeline: Activity › attention filter
failureModes: A summary always carries the ids of its underlying events so it stays traceable.
Attention events are never folded into a routine group.

A burst of same-cause checkout sync refusals (same checkout and reason within thirty minutes) reads as one attention row with a count; its event ids stay attached and Detailed shows each one, without any retry or rebase.
Condensation is deterministic, so repeated renders produce the same feed.

is deterministic and traceable to underlying event ids

features.title: Inspect verification receipts in the Activity Timeline
features.summary: Project Checks publishes a strict, bounded receipt summary after persistence; the timeline deduplicates replay, marks failures and timeouts for attention, and opens only a currently listed Session.
features.currentSurface: left-nav: Activity Timeline: Activity › receipt detail
failureModes: Unknown schema versions and extra payload fields are rejected before the timeline stores an event.
An archived or missing Session is reported unavailable without being revived or mutated.
A missing Activity Timeline does not prevent Project Checks from persisting its authoritative receipt.
Historical revisions are not presented as current source freshness, and configuration equivalence remains unknown.

externalDependencies.boundary: Versioned safe receipt summaries over the shared Activity event and bounded backfill events; Timeline never reads Project Checks storage.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Exercise schema, safe mapping, replay dedupe, and persistence ordering with fixed unit inputs and the scratch browser journey.

verification.testName: accepts only the current version and exact bounded fields

features.title: One attention inbox for everything that needs you
features.summary: Host-owned inbox items (reason, source, subject, severity, verbs, dedupe key) in the dshfiles_attention storage domain. Providers publish, resolve or reconcile through the attention-api module; the user and the Agent list, mark done, snooze (until a time or until it changes), reopen and mute a source; provider verbs such as Answer are handed to the owning plugin. Browsers follow a live changed event carrying the Needs you count.
features.currentSurface: Host contract: attention-api module and attention_* agent tools
failureModes: A repeat with the same source and dedupe key merges into one item instead of stacking; an unchanged repeat writes nothing.
A changed repeat lifts a snooze-until-change and a Done; a timed snooze holds until its time.
A resolved item reopens only when its source publishes it again; Reopen on a resolved item is refused with the reason.
Browsers and agents cannot publish, resolve or reconcile; those calls are refused as provider-only.
A provider verb with no loaded owner returns an outcome telling the user to open the thread instead of failing silently.
Info items never reach the inbox; they become one Activity log entry.
Closed items are pruned after seven days and the store is bounded at 2000 items.

externalDependencies.boundary: Provider through the attention-api module (publish/resolve/reconcile, dshfiles/attention/act); the inbox never reads its storage.

features.title: Inbox page with one Needs you badge
features.summary: An Inbox entry in the left navigation opens one page with Needs you and Other tabs (plus Snoozed, Done and Muted when they hold items). Each row shows a severity glyph, the reason, the source, a link to the thread and its verbs inline: answer choices, Open, Done, Snooze and Mute source, with Reopen and Unmute on the history tabs. The nav glyph carries the only badge, the Needs you count, and can raise opt-in browser alerts for blocking items.
failureModes: An archived or missing thread is reported unavailable with a recovery hint instead of being reopened.
A refused action (resolved item, no provider loaded) shows the provider message with what to do instead.
A disconnected event stream falls back to polling, so the badge still converges.
Browser alerts stay off until the user opts in and grants permission; a denied permission says how to allow it.
